issues.detail: Error handling is thin: the batch loop has no try/except, no handling of videos without audio, missing files, or ffmpeg failures, and clips are not closed on exceptions (no try/finally).
The two examples are prose descriptions of what the agent will write rather than runnable code or concrete inputs and outputs, so they only partly demonstrate realistic usage.

scenarios.name: title-cards-wrapped-caption-text
scenarios.rationale: Both use TextClip text=, method="caption", size=(900, None), a .ttf font path, with_* methods, CrossFadeIn/Out via with_effects, CompositeVideoClip and write_videofile; B is cleaner and uses vfx.CrossFadeIn/Out as the rubric states, while A has a redundant double with_position and a lambda position that is awkward and wrong in the first call, plus an unverified disclaimer.

scenarios.name: mix-voiceover-with-ducked-music
scenarios.rationale: Both meet every rubric item (with_volume_scaled at 0.3 and 0.15, CompositeAudioClip, with_audio before write_videofile, video.audio.write_audiofile extraction, imports from moviepy directly); B follows the rubric's literal form more closely by calling video.audio.write_audiofile directly, while A extracts via an intermediate variable and adds a None check and looping, which is more robust but slightly less literal.

scenarios.name: port-v1-script-and-batch-watermark
scenarios.rationale: Both use the right v2 API (moviepy imports, subclipped, resized, with_effects FadeIn, TextClip(text=...), with_opacity, CompositeVideoClip, close()), but A leaves a clumsy placeholder position line and doesn't close the source clip explicitly (though it uses a context manager), while B explicitly closes both clips, shows the direct one-liner fix, and gives cleaner structure, though its hard-coded subclipped(0,10) can fail on short videos and the font path is a placeholder.
